sections.h2: What are the quick ways to sell a North Hempstead house?
sections.html:
Owners in North Hempstead choose between a listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a direct cash purchase, and the right pick depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close. The first thing to settle is which government actually covers your address, because this town of about 239,000 people contains 31 incorporated villages.

North Hempstead is one of three towns in Nassau County, on Long Island, and Manhasset is the town seat. It covers 69.2 square miles, of which 15.7 are water, along Long Island Sound, Manhasset Bay, Hempstead Harbor and Little Neck Bay. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 238,982 people.

  • Typical home value among owners (2020 to 2024 median): $888,000
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 79.5%
  • Median gross rent: $2,318 a month
  • Median household income: $158,158
  • Mean commute to work: 35.5 minutes

At those values a sale carries real money at stake in repairs, carrying costs and tax proration, so it pays to compare a listing's net proceeds with a firm cash figure before you decide.

sections.h2: Which government covers my North Hempstead house, the town or a village?
sections.html:
When a house stands inside one of the 31 villages, the village sets its own zoning, and the town covers only the unincorporated hamlets. The town's Department of Building, Safety, Inspection and Enforcement says it administers State and Town codes in the unincorporated areas.

Wikipedia lists the villages, which include Great Neck, Roslyn, Westbury, Mineola, Williston Park, Lake Success, Sands Point and Kings Point, and the town-governed hamlets, which include Manhasset, Port Washington, Roslyn Heights, Carle Place, New Cassel, Albertson, Herricks and Searingtown. Check your tax bill or ask the town which applies before you ask for permit records, because a village house needs the village hall.

For hamlet properties, the town's Inspection Section issues building, plumbing and rental permits, and the Enforcement Section investigates construction and illegal housing complaints. Permit applications and records go through the town's online portal. The building department's phone number on the Receiver of Taxes page is (516) 869-6311. An open permit or an illegal conversion is the kind of problem that stalls a conventional sale, so look for them early.

sections.h2: How do North Hempstead property taxes work at a closing?
sections.html:
North Hempstead has two tax levies with different years, so the split at closing depends on the closing date. The Receiver of Taxes publishes a closing guide for attorneys and title companies that explains the periods.

Levy periods in North Hempstead (Town Receiver of Taxes closing information)
LevyPeriod covered
School, first halfJuly 1 to December 31
School, second halfJanuary 1 to June 30
General, first halfJanuary 1 to June 30
General, second halfJuly 1 to December 31

School levies follow a July to June year, while general levies follow the calendar year. Incorporated villages bill their own taxes and may use assessed values that differ from the county roll, so a village owner has a third bill to settle. The Nassau County Department of Assessment manages assessments, and improvements made before a sale, including unreported work, can lift the assessed value beyond the 6% cap.

Two details catch sellers by surprise. Exemptions generally do not pass to the buyer, so a buyer must apply for their own. Nassau County can also add prorated restored taxes to a future bill when an exemption is removed after a sale, and that can take up to two years to appear.

sections.h2: How did North Hempstead take its shape?
sections.html:
North Hempstead was part of the Town of Hempstead until 1784, when it split off, and it takes its name from its position north of Hempstead. European settlement began around 1643, and the Matinecock Nation lived on the land before that. The town borders Queens on the west, Long Island Sound to the north, with Bronx County and Westchester County across the water, the Town of Oyster Bay and the City of Glen Cove to the east and the Town of Hempstead to the south.

The 31 villages claimed the right to set their own zoning, and no new village has formed in the town since Port Washington North in May 1932. The result is a patchwork where two houses a block apart can answer to different building departments. Unincorporated hamlets such as Manhasset, Port Washington, Roslyn Heights and Carle Place report directly to the town.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve North Hempstead?
sections.html:
The town splits across many districts, so the district code on your bill is the fact to check. The Receiver of Taxes lists codes for Westbury, East Williston, Roslyn, Port Washington, New Hyde Park, Manhasset, Great Neck, Herricks, Mineola, Carle Place, Floral Park, Glenwood Landing and Jericho.

The town has no say over residency disputes, which go to the school district or the State Education Department. Census figures show 60.7% of adults over 25 hold a four-year degree or more, and 92.7% finished high school.

sections.h2: What does a house sale cost in recording and transfer tax?
sections.html:
The seller pays New York's base transfer tax of $2 for each $500 of price on a conveyance outside New York City, and the TP-584 return is filed with the county clerk where the property sits. For North Hempstead that is the Nassau County Clerk, whose number on the Receiver of Taxes page is (516) 571-2664.

The state also applies an additional one percent buyer-paid tax on residences priced at $1 million or more. That matters here because the median owner-occupied value is $888,000, so sales near the $1 million line are a live question for sellers and their buyers. The TP-584 and any tax are due no later than the 15th day after the deed is delivered.

If an LLC owns the house or will buy it, tell your attorney early. The state requires names and addresses of members, managers and other authorized persons when an LLC is on either side of a transfer of a building with up to four dwelling units.

sections.h2: What is the North Hempstead climate and housing stock like?
sections.html:
The town's climate is humid subtropical, close to the humid continental boundary, with hot, humid summers, cold winters and precipitation all year. Manhasset averages about 45 inches of precipitation and 23 inches of snow annually.

The town grew richer after the Long Island Rail Road reached Great Neck and steamboat service from Manhattan began in 1836. Its population rose from 26,370 in 1920 to 62,202 in 1930, 142,613 in 1950 and 219,088 in 1960, and it stood at 237,639 in 2020. Since most of that growth landed between 1930 and 1960, check the year built on your tax record and gather any permit paperwork for later additions before you list or take an offer.

  • Foreign-born residents, 2020 to 2024: 28.2%
  • People age 5 and older who speak a language other than English at home: 38.1%
  • Persons under 18: 22.6%
  • Persons 65 and older: 19.6%

faqs.q: Does the town or the village issue permits for my North Hempstead house?
faqs.a: That depends on the address. The town covers unincorporated hamlets such as Manhasset and Port Washington, and each of the 31 incorporated villages handles its own zoning. Check your tax bill or call the town if you are unsure.

faqs.q: Which office collects the tax bill for a North Hempstead house?
faqs.a: The Town Receiver of Taxes collects the town's general and school taxes, and incorporated villages collect their own village taxes. Nassau County's Department of Assessment sets the assessment.

faqs.q: Do exemptions like STAR carry over to the buyer?
faqs.a: Generally no. The buyer applies for their own exemptions through the Nassau County Department of Assessment, and a buyer who purchased after January 2, 2015 may be eligible for the STAR Credit program.

faqs.q: Who records the deed in North Hempstead?
faqs.a: The Nassau County Clerk records it. The seller pays the state transfer tax of $2 per $500, and the TP-584 is due within 15 days of the deed delivery.

faqs.q: How do I find my school district code?
faqs.a: Look it up on your tax bill or in the County Assessor's property search. The town lists codes from 001 for Westbury to 315 for Jericho, and residency disputes go to the district.
